transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. To get us started, could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. Well, what brings me in is... I'm having this issue with food at night. 

Once I start eating, it feels like I just can't stop. It's a strange feeling—it's almost like I can see myself doing it, and I'm in my head telling myself to just stop, but... my hands just keep going back for more. That's really what made me finally make the appointment.
During these episodes where you feel unable to stop eating, do you also feel a sense of distress or guilt afterward?

Yes, definitely. Afterward... it's just this heavy feeling of guilt. I feel terrible about what I've done, and it's really upsetting to realize I lost control like that again. It's a very distressing feeling, just sitting there knowing I couldn't stop myself.
Do these episodes of feeling like you cannot stop eating only happen at night, or do they also occur during the day?
It's pretty much just at night. During the day, I don't really have that issue. I haven't noticed myself losing control like that before the evening... so, yeah, it really just happens at night.
Do you find that these nighttime eating episodes are often accompanied by difficulty falling asleep or staying asleep?

No, I haven't really noticed any issues with that. I don't have trouble falling asleep or staying asleep. Once the... well, once the eating is done and I actually get into bed, I usually sleep just fine. So, no, my sleep hasn't really been a problem.
During those times you eat at night, do you feel like you are consuming a very large amount of food, or is it more like you are eating small amounts repeatedly throughout the evening?

It's definitely a large amount. I wouldn't call it just eating small amounts here and there. Some evenings, I’ll start with just some leftovers, but then... well, I end up eating sandwiches, cereal, cookies, and really whatever snack food is in the pantry. It ends up being far more than I would ever put on a plate for a normal supper.
After these episodes where you eat a large amount of food, do you ever do anything to try to compensate for the calories, such as vomiting, using laxatives, or exercising intensely?

Well, I don't do anything like making myself throw up or taking laxatives. But... yeah, I do try to make up for it in other ways. After a bad eating night, I’ll usually tell myself I need to balance it out, so I just skip breakfast and lunch the next day. 

And I do a lot of walking. I'll end up walking miles past my usual route to try and burn it off, even when my knees are really aching and telling me I should just head home. So, I guess I do push myself pretty hard to compensate that way.

When you decide to skip meals or exercise excessively after these episodes, is your primary motivation driven by an intense fear of gaining weight or a strong dissatisfaction with your body shape or weight?

Yes, it is. It's definitely about my body and my weight. 

I mean, I used to judge a good day by whether I solved a tough design problem at work, or maybe if I helped out down at the theater. But lately... well, I look at my stomach in the mirror, and I just feel like the whole measure of me is whether I look controlled or if I look sloppy. 

So, yeah, that dissatisfaction is exactly why I push myself to skip those meals and walk until my joints ache. I just really don't want to look out of control.
